findings.title: No re-check of the cache after taking the write lock
findings.body:
`GetWebAssets` reads the cache under `RLock`, releases it, then takes the exclusive `Lock`. It never re-checks `entryPointAssetsCache` after acquiring that lock.

When the cache is empty (startup, or after a failed load), every concurrent caller that saw `nil` queues on the write lock. Each one then re-reads and re-parses `assets-manifest.json` in turn, even though the first one already filled the cache.

This redundant reload can also lose a good value. If a later goroutine's reload fails (e.g. a transient read error), it sets `entryPointAssetsCache = result` with `nil`. That overwrites the valid cache the first goroutine just stored, and the caller gets an error that a simple re-check would have avoided.

Fix: after `Lock()`, add `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }`. Alternatively, only assign the cache when `err == nil`.
